paragraphs.text: How to use Napkin AI in one line: paste your text, click to generate a visual, pick the one that fits, edit it and export it. Napkin turns written text into flowcharts, mind maps, infographics, diagrams, data charts and slides, and you do not need to write a prompt or know design to use it. It runs in the browser, so there is nothing to install.

The free plan is real, not a trial. It gives you 500 AI credits a week, unlimited editing, unlimited file imports and unlimited PNG and PDF exports. The catch is that free visuals carry Napkin branding, and PowerPoint and SVG export need a paid plan.

That makes Napkin a good fit for one specific job: you already have the words, in a report, a lesson plan, a blog post or a slide, and you want a clean diagram next to them in a minute instead of an hour in a design app.
How to use Napkin AI, step by step

paragraphs.title: 1. Create a free account
paragraphs.text: Go to napkin.ai and sign up, or sign in with your Google account. Everything happens in a browser tab.

paragraphs.title: 2. Open a new napkin and add your text
paragraphs.text: Start a blank napkin and paste the text you want to turn into a visual. You can also import a file: the free plan takes PPT, DOC, PDF, HTML and Markdown files. If you only have an idea, you can describe it and let Napkin draft the text or an outline first.

Napkin's own site says no prompting is needed for this step. You paste normal text, not instructions for a picture. The Windows Club makes the same point in its walkthrough: paste a summary or a paragraph, not a description of the image you want.

paragraphs.title: 3. Click the spark icon next to a paragraph
paragraphs.text: Hover over a block of text until a small spark icon appears beside it, then click it. Napkin reads that text and shows several visual options built from your own words.

paragraphs.title: 4. Pick a visual and a style
paragraphs.text: Scroll through the options and choose the one that fits. Then try other styles for the same visual until the colors and layout suit where it will go.

paragraphs.title: 5. Edit anything
paragraphs.text: Nothing is locked after generation. Click text to change the words, font or size, change colors, swap icons, change the layout, or reshape single elements. Data charts stay editable too.

paragraphs.title: 6. Export it
paragraphs.text: Download the visual as PNG or PDF on the free plan. Paid plans add PowerPoint and SVG. Napkin says the result can go into PowerPoint, Google Slides, Canva, Keynote, Google Docs, Word, Notion, blogs and social posts.
Fast.io's review adds one gap worth knowing: Napkin does not connect directly to Google Slides, Notion or Figma, so in practice you export a file and import it yourself.
Text that turns into good Napkin visuals

Napkin reads the structure of your text. Numbered steps tend to become flowcharts, and a short line on each option becomes a side by side comparison. Fast.io's review found that bullet points, numbered lists and outlines with headings work best, while dense, unstructured prose produces generic or confused visuals.
Write the idea the way you would explain it out loud, in short lines. Then paste it. One clear idea per paragraph gives Napkin one clear visual per spark icon.

paragraphs.title: Text to paste: a process that becomes a flowchart
paragraphs.text:
How we handle a customer refund:
1. The customer fills in the refund form.
2. Support checks the order number within 24 hours.
3. If the item was used, a manager approves or declines.
4. Finance sends the money back within 5 business days.
5. The customer gets a confirmation email.

paragraphs.title: Text to paste: options that become a comparison
paragraphs.text:
Three ways to learn Spanish this year:
App: cheap and flexible, but easy to quit.
Evening class: fixed schedule and a teacher, but slower.
Tutor online: fastest progress, but the most expensive.

paragraphs.title: Text to paste: a topic that becomes a mind map
paragraphs.text: Planning a small wedding: venue, guest list, budget, food, music, photos, clothes, travel for family.
Replace these examples with your own steps, options or topic. The shape of the text matters more than the subject.
Napkin AI free plan, credits and prices

Napkin charges AI credits for generating visuals, at about one credit per word you select, according to its pricing page. More complex outputs can cost more. Fast.io's review says the 500 free weekly credits reset every Monday. Editing does not use credits, and you can buy more credits or upgrade when you run out.

The pricing page lists Plus at $9 per person per month with 10,000 credits a month, no Napkin branding, PowerPoint and SVG export and 3 brand styles. Pro is $22 per person per month with 30,000 credits, unlimited custom branding and font uploads. The page says paying yearly saves 25 percent, and Fast.io lists the month to month prices as $12 and $30, so check which billing option is selected before you pay. Napkin says it offers no student or nonprofit discounts.

On privacy, the pricing page says anonymized interaction data from self-serve accounts may be used to improve its AI, and that you can opt out in Account Settings. Enterprise customer data is not used for training.
What Napkin AI is bad at

Napkin draws confident, polished figures whether or not they are correct. One writer who uses it for medical teaching material warns that it can mislabel boxes, merge steps, or draw arrows that suggest links your text never stated. Fast.io also found that layouts can look repetitive across different inputs, and that abstract topics without concrete facts give vague diagrams.

It also makes single visuals first. Napkin Slides is still labeled beta on the company's site, and visual generation is not yet available on mobile, although you can view and edit existing work there.
Read every label and every arrow before you use a Napkin visual in anything that matters. If the diagram says something your text does not, fix the arrow or delete it.

The honest verdict: Napkin is fast and the free plan covers casual use, but the watermark and the PNG and PDF only export push regular users toward a paid plan. For a quick diagram in a doc or a post, it saves real time. For a full deck or a precise technical drawing, use a dedicated tool.
